$comment: Lines a conforming client must accept even though they are not canonical. These exist because the protocol evolves additively: a shell built against an older service has to keep working when a newer one adds a field, and refusing what it does not recognise is the failure mode that turns an additive change into a breaking one.

cases.name: unknown-field-in-envelope
cases.why: A field added by a newer service. It is ignored, not refused.

cases.name: unknown-field-in-payload
cases.why: The same, one level down. Payload growth is the common case.

cases.name: absent-optional-payload-fields
cases.why: Everything optional omitted at once, which is what a minimal acknowledgement looks like.

cases.name: request-payload-omitted-entirely
cases.why: `payload` carries a serde default, so a sender may leave it out even though this crate always writes it.

cases.name: future-protocol-version
cases.why: A version string is data, not a gate at the parsing layer. Deciding whether 0.4.0 is acceptable belongs to the compatibility check, which can only run once the frame has been read.
